text: Agreed to pace rolling endurance rides steadily on climbs rather than surge, using conversational breathing and comfortable cadence to control effort through the middle hours.
The final riser felt unusually hard into a headwind after a long day on the feet; this was judged situational rather than evidence of declining fitness.
For exposed headwinds, agreed to tuck lower and move snacks earlier to preserve final-hour energy, while monitoring hands and shoulders as low-position duration and weekly volume increase.
Mild heaviness on day two of back-to-back rides cleared after 20 minutes of easy spinning, so the plan remains unchanged; if it persists beyond 30 minutes, the second ride will be shortened.
Set a fueling routine for rides over two hours: one bottle per hour, food every 30 minutes, and a larger breakfast before sustained climbing; practice it first on easy rides.
Recovery spins will start from the park side of town because fewer junctions make easy pacing easier; these rides will remain protected when the schedule is busy.
